case_title: Rambir v. State of NCT, Delhi
accused_socioeconomic_status: Not stated (judgment records only that the appellant's counsel was appointed by the Delhi High Court Legal Services Committee)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.34 (as cited in FIR); conviction under IPC s.302, modified to s.304 Part II
evidence_type: Eyewitness testimony (son), last-seen evidence (PW-9), witness corroboration (PW-17, PW-18), scene evidence (PW-15 found body with saria)
mitigating_circumstances: Sudden fight, no premeditation, act in heat of passion, manner not extremely cruel
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 IPC; sentenced to life imprisonment
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed (judgment dated 11.10.2017); conviction under s.302 and life sentence confirmed
offence_finally_established: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder, IPC s.304 Part II (Exception 4 to s.300)
neutral_facts: On the intervening night of 31 August and 1 September 2010, the accused is alleged to have strangled the victim, his wife, on the rooftop of a residential premises in Delhi, causing her death. The primary eyewitness was the couple's son, who testified that he saw the accused strangling his mother with an iron rod (saria) after she had taken money from the accused's wallet. The son's account was the central prosecution evidence. A police sub-inspector, the first officer to reach the scene, found the victim's body on the terrace along with a saria, an empty liquor bottle and a plastic glass. A worker in the workshop on the premises testified that he saw the accused leaving the premises in the morning of 1 September 2010. Two further prosecution witnesses confirmed the accused's presence at the scene. The case was registered as an FIR on 1 September 2010 under sections 302 and 34 of the Penal Code. The investigation and trial relied on these eyewitness, last-seen and scene-based evidence, together with the recovered rod.
physical_harm: Death of victim by strangulation with a saria
number_of_offences: 1 charged (s.302 IPC, with s.34 cited in FIR); 1 finally upheld (s.304 Part II IPC, conviction modified)
premeditation_planning: No premeditation found; the court held the saria was picked up on the spur of the moment
motive: Sudden quarrel after the victim took money from the accused's wallet (court accepted incident arose in a sudden fight)
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness testimony of PW-7 (son); corroboration by PW-9 (last seen leaving), PW-17 and PW-18 (presence), and PW-15 (scene and saria)
witness_credibility: High Court found PW-7, PW-9, PW-17 and PW-18 credible and reliable; Supreme Court accepted PW-7's account as the basis for finding a sudden fight
post_offence_conduct: Accused seen leaving the premises at about 6:30 a.m. on 1 September 2010 (PW-9); no other conduct noted
trial_duration: offence: 31.08.2010 and 01.09.2010 (intervening night); trial judgment: 19.07.2012; High Court: 11.10.2017; Supreme Court: 06.05.2019
legal_representation: Appellant: Shikhil Suri, Shiv Kumar Suri (Advocates). State: Ms. Pinky Anand, ASG, with Ashok Panigrahi, P. S. Sudheer, Ms. Kirti Dua, B.V. Balaram Das (Advocates)
investigation_status: FIR registered 01.09.2010; 18 prosecution witnesses examined; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.302, life imprisonment (23.07.2012). High Court: appeal dismissed (11.10.2017). Supreme Court: appeal partly allowed; conviction modified to s.304 Part II, 10 years' simple imprisonment
prosecution_argument: Clear murder proved by four witnesses; compressing the neck with a saria cannot be an act committed in a fit of anger; strangulation with a saria is an extremely cruel act, so Exception 4 is rightly negated
defence_argument: Sudden quarrel in a fit of anger under influence of liquor; no intention to kill; all four ingredients of Exception 4 to s.300 IPC are met, and the High Court's finding on two ingredients runs contrary to evidence
legal_principle_applied: Four ingredients of Exception 4 to s.300 IPC; strangulation is not extreme cruelty unless barbaric, torturous and brutal
precedent_relied_upon: Surinder Kumar v. Union Territory, Chandigarh (1989) 2 SCC 217 : [1989] 1 SCR 941
sentencing_rationale: Act committed in sudden fight and heat of passion without premeditation and not extremely cruel, so Exception 4 applies; conviction reduced to s.304 Part II with 10 years' simple imprisonment
judicial_mitigating_factors: Sudden quarrel; no premeditation; act in heat of passion; manner not extremely cruel
